summary: The retained diagnostics toggle-evidence helper is off-to-off only on its success path. After enable(lab), enabled-window canonical capture/comparison assertions execute before disable(lab); any error in that interval exits runToggleEvidence() with the owned diagnostics overlay still live until an explicit cleanup or a later helper start. This is distinct from enable() transaction rollback and from the generation-13 clone-completeness repair.
evidence: Inspected integration-ready diagnostics PR #432 exact head 7716eba2ace4be9dc04df7264a1003de5dc0df55 after checking existing diagnostics PR/issue lineage for a duplicate cleanup repair.

runToggleEvidence() calls PhysicsLabStudioDiagnostics.enable(lab), then captureCanonicalWhileDiagnosticsEnabled(lab), Validation.compare(), zero-delta assertions, and the enabled-envelope assertion before its first PhysicsLabStudioDiagnostics.disable(lab) for that cycle.

Those enabled-window operations are not inside an outer protected cleanup boundary. A thrown capture/comparison/assertion therefore bypasses the later disable call and leaves the diagnostics Folder created by successful enable() parented under the live lab model.

tests/physics_lab_diagnostics_enabled_integrity.luau explicitly locks enable -> enabled canonical capture -> compare -> delta/envelope checks -> disable ordering, but it does not require a failure-path cleanup/finalizer around that interval.

The next runToggleEvidence() invocation starts with disable(lab), so the defect is bounded and recoverable; the issue is that the failed invocation itself does not satisfy final-OFF/fail-closed cleanup and can leave operator-visible diagnostic state after an evidence failure.

Search of diagnostics PRs/issues found enabled-canonical clone cleanup, enable() rollback, represented-set integrity, and bounded-cycle work, but no separate runToggleEvidence enabled-window failure-cleanup repair.

metadata.recommendedNext: After current diagnostics integration sequencing is safe, add one bounded diagnostics leaf that preserves enabled-window validation-before-disable semantics but guarantees owned-overlay cleanup on every post-enable error path, preserves the original evidence failure when cleanup succeeds, reports cleanup failure without masking ownership state, and adds a regression that rejects success-path-only cleanup. Do not claim Studio PASS from the source repair.
